name: Tlachichilco Tepehua
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Watters, James K. 1980. Aspects of Tlachichilco Tepehua (Totonacan) Phonology; Watters 1988. Topics in Tepehua Grammar. PhD diss., UC Berkeley

new_statements.quote: 3.1 Each word in TT has one stressed syllable. [...] While there is no consistent placement of stress on other parts of speech, stress occurs on the verb according to the following rule: R24 stress placement [...] A vowel is stressed when it is separated from the clitic boundary by a following syllable and the following syllable a) contains a short vowel and is closed by a noncontinuant, or, b) is an open syllable with a short vowel. If it is in a syllable immediately preceding the clitic boundary, a vowel is stressed a) when it is followed by a continuant, and/or, b) when it is [+long].
new_statements.citation: Watters, James. 1980. Aspects of Tlachichilco Tepehua (Totonacan) phonology. SIL Mexico Workpapers 4: 85-129.
new_statements.locator: sec. 3.1, p. 100 (first sentence) and sec. 4, p. 105 (R24 stress placement and its prose statement); stress shift R31 on p. 111
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (38-page image scan, Rosetta Project item rosettaproject_tpt_phon-1/-2 on archive.org; re-checked today via web lookups as public, no access restriction). I rendered PDF pages 2, 3, 16, 21, 27, 28 (= printed pp. 86, 87, 100, 105, 111, 112) and read them against the scanned ( lines 1966-1972, 2632-2653, 3800-3837, 4011-4017). Every part of the quoted passage is on the page exactly as quoted: p. 100 "3.1 Each word in TT has one stressed syllable. In polysyllabic words all pre-stress syllables are mid-pitch and the stressed and post-stress syllables are high-pitch (unless preceding pause)..."; p. 105 "While there is no consistent placement of stress on other parts of speech, stress occurs…
new_statements.rule_in_words: One stressed syllable per word. In verbs (the only part of speech for which Watters gives a rule) stress is on the final syllable before the clitic boundary when that syllable has a long vowel or is closed by a continuant consonant (e.g. -w, -y, -n, -l, fricatives); otherwise, when the final syllable has a short vowel and is open or closed by a stop/affricate, stress is on the penult. For nouns and other parts of speech the source says placement is not consistent (i.e. lexically unpredictable as far as this description goes).
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned; the source states one stressed syllable per word and describes pitch (pre-stress syllables mid, stressed and post-stress syllables high, except before pause).
new_statements.exceptions: R31 stress shift (p. 111): when a stressed vowel immediately precedes the punctiliar suffix -li, stress moves to the vowel of the preceding syllable unless that syllable is a clitic; the completive suffix -?o: is listed as the only exception to R31 (p. 112). Stress on non-verbs: 'no consistent placement'. Verbs with the 2nd-person -t?i suffix undergo R26 before R24 (p. 107).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (verb) delimited by the clitic boundary; in normal and fast speech word boundaries are deleted and pitch patterns over the phrase, but each word's stressed syllable retains its stress (p. 100). Data are citation/derivational forms in an SPE-style rule analysis; no instrumental study.
new_statements.identity_note: Watters 1980 describes 'TT' = Tlachichilco Tepehua 'spoken in the municipio of Tlachichilco, Veracruz and in seven surrounding villages' (p. 86, fn. 2), i.e. tlac1235 itself, not a differently named variety; he treats Pisaflores (pisa1244) and Huehuetla (hueh1236) as the other two Tepehua dialects. Kung 2007 and Herrera 2021 (held under hueh1236) describe Huehuetla/Mecapalapa Tepehua and were consulted only for cross-references.

Sec. 4 p. 105 R24: no consistent stress placement on non-verbs; in the verb a vowel is stressed in the final syllable (before the clitic boundary) when followed by a continuant and/or when long, otherwise in the syllable before a final syllable that has a short vowel and is open or closed by a noncontinuant (i.e. final-if-heavy, else penult). sources.note: Different language (Mecapalapa variety of Huehuetla Tepehua). Says Mecapalapa stress is predictable and non-contrastive, penult or final.
